failure_summary.description: A filled `optional parameters` list was followed by a second empty `"optional parameters": []` key. This erased enable (education:23), page (education:72) and get_test (education:28). The skill already shows this exact bad string four times.

A plausible-looking generic tool was chosen over the literal fit: lat/lng Airbnb instead of the admin-divisions tool (travel:7), BizToc instead of the movie-news tool (news:1), and Disposable Email Validation instead of Email Existence Validator (email:115).

Required and optional were mixed up: Aliexpress q/startPrice/region were put in required although the schema's required list is none (ecommerce:21), DEI `page` was put in optional although the schema lists it as required (education:72), and starid was put in required (education:28). Value defaults were also wrong (Asos lang `en`, Amazon domain `US`).
Narrative query lost the kanji 'parent' facet and the final Uncovered Treasure search clause (education:23).
Wrote `Lost Ark — get classes` although the heading and the query both use `Lost Ark: get classes`. The skill's own BAD example (`Lost Ark — get engravings`) is nearly identical to the output.

patch.reasoning: The agent answers directly with no visible reasoning, so process rules (checklists, skeleton passes) are not executed. Step 17's rejection shows that quoting a bad string in the skill makes the model reproduce it (the `], "},` example came back verbatim). The fast section prints the duplicate-key bad string three more times, and it prints a dash-name BAD example that closely matches the one dash failure here. These edits remove the priming strings and replace them with positive one-line statements. Each rule shrinks, none grows, and the slow block's single copy of the bad pattern stays. Layout, skeleton and one-object-per-line rules are left untouched because the last three epochs showed changing them hurts. Tool-selection and placement misses repeat rules the skill already states, and the meta guidance says not to restate them or chase per-tool placement flips.
